item.title: Scientists coated a cicada wing with silver and created a sensor that amplified molecular signals
item.description: Researchers developed a sensitive optical sensor using cicada wings and silver. This natural structure boosts weak molecular signals significantly, replacing expensive manufacturing. Silver coating on cicada wings creates tiny gaps that amplify light signals. This technology could lead to portable sensors for detecting pollution and toxins. Future studies will test these sensors with real-world environmental and medical samples.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar loses Democratic primary in Michigan
item.description: Shri Thanedar lost the Michigan Democratic primary to Donavan McKinney. McKinney secured victory with support from the party's progressive wing. Thanedar acknowledged the socialist movement's influence on the election outcome. His defeat may reduce Indian-American representation in the House. Thanedar expressed gratitude for his service and plans to remain active.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Inside bassist Flea’s $8M Malibu home
item.description: The renowned bassist for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Flea, has placed his sought-after Malibu estate back on the market, currently commanding a price of $7.99 million. This elegant four-bedroom beachfront abode was once offered for monthly rent at $75,000. Additionally, Flea encountered difficulties while trying to sell another of his Californian residences, famed for its design by Richard Neutra, underlining the allure of this exclusive coastal community.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: UBC scientists develop a mixture that keep strawberries fresh
item.description: In an exciting advancement, scientists have created an edible seaweed coating that dramatically prolongs the freshness of fruits, particularly strawberries, even at room temperature—outperforming typical refrigeration. This innovative method not only safeguards vital nutrients but also possesses antibacterial features that benefit produce. By adopting this approach, we can significantly cut down on food waste and reduce environmental impact, offering a sustainable alternative to existing cold storage techniques.

item.title: An 11-year-old autistic boy wanted to trick-or-treat in summer; neighbors opened their doors and...
item.description: A heartfelt Facebook post from a mother seeking birthday cheer for her autistic son ignited an incredible wave of community support. Eighty-three families joined in a unique summer trick-or-treat celebration for Soren, showering him with handcrafted gifts and candies. This touching event not only spread joy but also shed light on the importance of acceptance, dismantling stereotypes associated with autism and showcasing the strength of community bonds.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Seungah Chung, the US eighth-grader who used 200 ants to discover landmark navigation
item.description: A bright young student embarked on a fascinating ant navigation experiment fueled by her natural curiosity. Through her meticulous research, she uncovered that ants primarily depend on visual markers for navigation. This groundbreaking project garnered her acclaim at a well-regarded science competition, showcasing the potential of such findings to inspire the development of innovative robots and autonomous systems.

item.title: Stacy Brooks expected to dislike downtown Minneapolis, but a one-year trial changed her mind
item.description: Stacy Brooks, originally from northern Minnesota, discovered a newfound happiness in her urban high-rise. After a year-long experiment, she and her husband are in the process of purchasing their 19th-floor apartment. Their daily routine transformed into leisurely walks, indulging in community amenities, and savoring a variety of local dining options. The supportive community of childfree neighbors further enhanced her experience, marking a significant departure from her previous suburban life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump's immigration crackdown hits US military families; over 50 spouses, parents detained
item.description: Dozens of parents and spouses of US service members face detention and deportation. This marks a significant shift from prior bipartisan immigration policies for military families. Many are detained during routine immigration status adjustment appointments. The Department of Homeland Security states military service does not exempt violations of immigration laws. These detentions negatively impact military readiness and family stability.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Texas uses discarded Christmas trees to help sea turtles survive
item.description: Discarded Christmas trees are repurposed to build sand dunes along the Texas coast. These trees are placed on beaches to trap shifting sand and strengthen the shoreline. This process occurs before the sea turtle nesting season begins each year. The new dunes provide a protective barrier for relocated sea turtle eggs. This initiative helps ensure a safer environment for hatchlings during their development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California will close the westbound Zampa Bridge for 53 hours to replace part of its deck
item.description: Important notice for travelers: Westbound access on the Al Zampa Memorial Bridge will be entirely shut down for 53 hours, commencing on Friday, August 21, and concluding on Monday, August 24, to facilitate necessary repairs. Motorists are urged to anticipate heavy delays and to follow detour signs. Please be advised that foot and bicycle traffic will also be halted during this repair window. Prepare your travel plans accordingly.
